name: Ironveil Chrome-Splice Street Rig
description: On the Shelf, salvaged augmentation hardware gets repurposed — not always for function, sometimes for identity. This outfit is built around that principle. The base is a sleeveless ribbed tank in dark gray thermal synth-cotton, its back cut open along the spine in a wide channel sealed with hook-and-loop closures — aug-compatible for spinal rig wearers, though this particular wearer uses the channel to route a non-functional decorative spine rail salvaged from a discarded medical-grade aug frame. The chrome piece runs from the mid-back to just below the neck, its surface scratched and dull, a few indicator lights that no longer illuminate. Over the tank, an open-front vest in black faux-leather hangs loose, its lapels weighted with salvaged circuit board fragments wired together as decorative trim — green PCB against black synthetic, soldered at the edges. The arms are bare from the shoulder, exposing a left arm with two chrome band prosthetic segments just below the elbow — functional, basic-grade, the housing scuffed and re-painted matte black with what appears to be spray paint. The right arm is fully biological, tattooed in dense black geometric patterns from wrist to shoulder that echo the circuit board trim on the vest. High-waist trousers in stiff dark indigo canvas are belted with a wide industrial webbing belt bearing five utility clips. Boots are heavy platform-soled lace-ups in black synthetic leather, the platform built up with layers of cut rubber sheeting and wrapped in black tape — DIY height, DIY intimidation. The face is half-obscured by a single-lens optical piece — not a full BCI visor, just a salvaged single ocular unit worn over the left eye, its housing cracked but the lens still tinted gold.
functionality: Spinal channel accommodates aug rigs or decorative hardware. Open-front vest allows rapid layering removal. Aug-compatible arm construction accommodates prosthetic right up to elbow joint with full shoulder mobility. Utility belt clips carry tools and small gear. Platform soles add height and protect feet from chemical pooling on Shelf grating. Single ocular unit provides basic light filtering in bright industrial zones.
what_it_says: Chrome is status on the Shelf — not because it means wealth, but because it means you've dealt with something serious enough to require replacement parts and survived it. The decorative use of salvaged aug hardware says this wearer understands the aesthetics of augmentation even without the budget for functional upgrades. The mix of biological tattoo patterns and chrome trim is a statement: flesh and machine, both marked, both deliberate.
worn_by: young Shelf residents building an identity around aug culture
manufacturer: Vest base: unknown street label; chrome hardware: salvaged aug surplus; remainder self-assembled
story_hooks: The decorative spine rail is recognized by a Lazarus MedCore technician as part of a spinal stabilization frame from a patient who was discharged three years ago and never returned for the hardware — the patient's file is flagged as a missing persons case.

The cracked gold-lens ocular unit, despite its broken housing, is still partially active and has been passively logging visual data for an unknown network — someone has been watching through this wearer's eye without their knowledge.

A Shelf chrome trader offers an unexpectedly large sum for the PCB circuit board trim on the vest lapels — not for the boards themselves, but for a single chip soldered among them that the wearer assumed was dead.

physical_description.visual_profile: A striking asymmetrical silhouette that reads as street-salvage haute couture. The figure presents as deliberately unfinished—part medical rig, part scrapyard fashion statement. Bare shoulders and exposed augmentation create a deliberately vulnerable-aggressive posture. The overall impression is survival-coded rebellion: nothing matches, everything communicates.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately loose and layered. The sleeveless tank sits close; the vest hangs open and oversized. High-waisted trousers create verticality and stance. Nothing is tailored—everything is worn, arranged, displayed rather than fitted.
physical_description.primary_material: Thermal synth-cotton base (tank), faux-leather (vest), treated indigo canvas (trousers), salvaged chrome hardware (spine rail, prosthetic segments), circuit board fragments (PCB trim), industrial webbing (belt), synthetic leather and rubber composite (boots)
physical_description.texture: Mixed and intentionally discordant. Smooth chrome dulled by scratches and oxidation. Soft cotton-weave ribbed surface. Stiff, unworn canvas. Rough, hand-soldered circuit boards. Weathered faux-leather with visible creasing. Wrapped rubber platforms taped and re-taped. Matte-black spray paint over polished prosthetic housing.
physical_description.color_scheme: Base palette of charcoal gray, black, and deep indigo. Accent colors: tarnished chrome (silver-gray), green PCB trim, gold-tinted lens, matte black overspray. High contrast between organic and synthetic elements.
physical_description.closures: Hook-and-loop closures on spine channel (functional, not fastened in this wear). Vest is open-front, no closures. Industrial webbing belt with clip buckles. Laced platform boots. Optical piece worn over eye without visible fastener (adhesive or friction-fit).
distinctive_features: Open-back spine channel with non-functional decorative chrome spine rail as centerpiece
Salvaged circuit board fragments (green PCB) soldered and wired as lapel trim
Left arm: two matte-black spray-painted chrome prosthetic band segments below elbow (functional, basic-grade)
Right arm: dense black geometric tattoo sleeve (biological, intentional contrast to left aug)
Single salvaged ocular unit worn over left eye, gold-tinted lens, cracked housing
Industrial webbing belt with five utility clips (empty or holding non-visible gear)
Platform boots built from layered rubber sheeting, hand-wrapped in black tape
Exposed augmentation hardware throughout—medical-grade salvage repurposed as identity
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 street/sub-grade. The outfit signals no access to corpo-grade augmentation or designer synth-wear. Every piece is salvaged, repurposed, or self-assembled. Value lies in assembly philosophy and cultural coding, not material cost.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street-tier body modification culture. Wearer signals: aug-compatible infrastructure, familiarity with salvage markets, deliberate rejection of mainstream corpo fashion, medical/industrial tech literacy. The mix of functional and non-functional chrome reads as identity-through-hardware—claiming augmentation as style as much as necessity. Tattoo sleeve on biological arm suggests cultural continuity across biological/synthetic divide.
physical_description.condition_typical: Intentionally worn-in and broken. Chrome should show oxidation and scratch marks from use. Paint on prosthetics shows wear and chip. Boots are scuffed and tape is peeling in places. PCB trim shows solder drips and oxidation. Vest leather has creases and potential minor tears. The optical lens is cracked but clear enough to see through. Nothing is pristine; wear is the point.
